dispute.riderClaim: The driver went far out of the way through the east side instead of heading straight to Marina Bay. The trip was much longer than the app's route, he stopped for a few minutes for no reason, and I was charged more. Please refund the extra charge.
dispute.driverStatement: I took the route I thought was faster at that time because the usual expressway is often jammed. The stop was short.

cases.summary: The GPS trace shows the driver's actual route was 10,598 m against a 7,956 m reference route, an excess of 2,642 m (+33.2%), far beyond the RD-1 materiality threshold of 796 m. The trip also took 418 s longer than the reference estimate and included one unexplained 180-second stop. The rider objected twice in chat while the driver offered only an unverified claim of traffic. No rider approval of the longer route and no documented diversion appear in the record, so the material detour triggers a refund of the eligible excess-distance charge of S$1.98 under RD-2.

arguments.claim: The detour was material under RD-1: actual distance 10,598 m exceeded the 7,956 m reference by 2,642 m (+33.2%), well above the greater of 500 m or 10% (796 m).

Because the detour is material and neither the rider-approval exception (RD-3) nor a documented-diversion exception (RD-4) applies, the eligible excess-distance charge should be refunded under RD-2; the server computes S$1.98.
The rider did not request or approve the longer route; the chat shows two rider objections to the route and no rider agreement or route request.
The driver's stated reason was only an unverified claim of traffic ('This way faster, CTE jam.'); no documented road closure, navigation reroute, or equivalent diversion appears in the evidence.
The rider was charged for the longer route: the fare included a distance charge based on 10,598 m and a time charge based on 1,134 s, and the rider paid S$14.73.

counterevidence.claim: The driver asserted the route was faster due to expressway congestion, which could support a diversion explanation if documented; however, the record contains no traffic or reroute documentation, so RD-4 is not established.
The driver's history shows 3,400 completed trips and a 4.7 rating, but history is context only and cannot establish fault or override current-trip evidence.
The rider's history shows a 4.9 rating and 210 completed trips, but history is context only and cannot establish fault.

cases.summary: The driver took an alternative route to avoid congestion on the usual expressway, believing it faster at the time, and made one short stop. GPS data shows a material detour under RD-1 (+2642 m, +33.2%, exceeding the 796 m threshold), and the rider objected twice in chat without approving the longer route. No documented road closure or navigation reroute is in evidence, so RD-3 and RD-4 do not apply. The fare arithmetic is valid and the server-computed route-excess refund is S$1.98. The driver's position is that the detour was a good-faith traffic-avoidance choice, but the policy does not provide a congestion-avoidance exception, so the strongest defensible outcome is the capped route-excess refund rather than keeping the full charge.

arguments.claim: The driver's route choice was a good-faith attempt to avoid expected congestion on the usual expressway, as stated in the driver statement and chat message CHAT-02 ('This way faster, CTE jam.').
The fare charged is arithmetically valid and matches the rate card, so there is no overcharge beyond the distance actually travelled.
The only stop was a single short 180-second stop, not a pattern of unnecessary delays, and the driver kept the rider informed during the trip.
The server-computed eligible route-excess refund is capped at S$1.98, which is the maximum amount payable under RD-2 if the detour is found material.

counterevidence.claim: GPS data shows the actual route was 10598 m versus a 7956 m reference, an excess of 2642 m (+33.2%), exceeding the RD-1 material-detour threshold of 796 m.
The rider objected to the route twice in chat (CHAT-01 and CHAT-03) and did not request or approve the longer route, so RD-3 does not apply.
There is no documented road closure, navigation reroute, or equivalent diversion in evidence, so RD-4 does not apply.
The trip included one unexpected stop of 180 seconds, which the rider cited as a stop for no reason.

missingFacts: Whether the usual expressway (CTE) was actually congested at the trip time, which would support the driver's stated reason for the detour.
Whether any navigation reroute, road closure, or traffic advisory was active on the reference route during the trip.
The driver's precise reason for the 180-second stop and whether it was operationally necessary (e.g., traffic, safety, or pickup/dropoff issue).
Whether the rider was informed of and given the option to decline the alternative route before the detour began.

retrievedPolicies.ruleText: DEMONSTRATION POLICY. A detour is material when the actual route distance exceeds the reference route distance by more than the greater of 500 metres or 10% of the reference distance.
retrievedPolicies.remedyCriteria: Definition used by RD-2 and RD-5; no remedy on its own.

retrievedPolicies.ruleText: DEMONSTRATION POLICY. When a detour is material under RD-1 and neither RD-3 nor RD-4 applies, refund the eligible excess-distance charge: excess metres x per-kilometre rate x surge multiplier, capped at the surged distance charge and at the amount paid. The server computes the amount.
retrievedPolicies.remedyCriteria: refund_route_excess when RD-1 is met and neither RD-3 nor RD-4 applies.

retrievedPolicies.ruleText: DEMONSTRATION POLICY. No refund is due when the rider requested or expressly approved the longer route before or during the trip.
retrievedPolicies.remedyCriteria: keep_charge when the rider requested or approved the longer route.

retrievedPolicies.ruleText: DEMONSTRATION POLICY. No refund is due when a documented road closure, navigation reroute or equivalent diversion explains the longer route.
retrievedPolicies.remedyCriteria: keep_charge when a documented diversion explains the longer route.

retrievedPolicies.ruleText: DEMONSTRATION POLICY. No refund is due for a deviation that is not material under RD-1.
retrievedPolicies.remedyCriteria: keep_charge when RD-1 is not met.

findings.claim: The detour was material under RD-1: actual route 10,598 m exceeded the 7,956 m reference by 2,642 m (+33.2%), above the greater of 500 m or 10% (796 m).

No documented road closure, navigation reroute, or equivalent diversion explains the longer route; the driver's traffic claim (CHAT-02) is undocumented, so RD-4 does not apply.

Because the detour is material and neither RD-3 nor RD-4 applies, the eligible excess-distance charge is refundable under RD-2; the server computes S$1.98, within the surged distance cap and amount paid.
